title: Pager throttling, dynamic runbook generation, and incident automation for SLO-driven multi-region failovers
creator: Lena Hoffman
description: Summary: Reduce noisy pages for transient infra events while ensuring timely operator action for SLO breaches and multi-region failovers. Implement a three-part solution: (1) pager throttling rules that are SLO-aware and robust to bursty token traffic; (2) dynamic runbook generation that composes the correct playbook for the failing service, region, and active circuit-breaker policy; (3) incident automation that can execute safe load-shedding and failover actions with human-in-the-loop escalation windows. Background: Recent incidents showed frequent low-urgency pages from model-serving tail latency spikes and cache warm-up storms that drown out real SLO violations. Existing playbooks are static and often outdated for newer runtime variants and dedicated/dedicated-private routing. Goals: Reduce page volume by 60% without increasing time-to-detect for true SLO breaches; ensure runbooks are accurate and executable per-region; automate common safe mitigation steps (prefix cache flush, scale burst, route to warm pool, circuit-breaker trip) with clear escalation. Non-goals: This ticket does not implement a new alerting backend; it changes rules and automations within the existing alerting stack and autoscaler hooks. Acceptance criteria: 1) Pager volume for non-actionable alerts drops >=60% on staging synthetic workload while true SLO violation alerts maintain or improve MTTA/MTTR in chaos tests. 2) Automated runbook generator produces a human-readable step list and the corresponding CLI commands for at least JVM and GPU runtime variants; validated by runbook review. 3) Automated mitigation can perform one of three actions (re-route to warm pool, initiate load-shedding with rate-limit policy, or trigger dedicated pool scale-up) and requires explicit manual confirm if cross-region failover is the outcome. 4) All actions produce audit events in central logging and a GitHub PR template is created for any runbook changes. Design notes and trade-offs: - Pager throttling uses an SLO-driven hysteresis window: alerts are suppressed for short transient metric bursts if aggregated SLO risk across shards is below threshold. Trade-off: slight detection latency for tiny transient spikes in favor of noise reduction. - Dynamic runbook generation pulls service metadata from the service catalog and the model-variant matrix to produce tailored steps. Trade-off: Adds a coupling between the catalog and runbook generator; mitigation: fall back to a curated generic playbook if metadata is missing. - Automations are implemented as idempotent, reversible steps with a default 'dry-run' flag for first rollouts. Trade-off: Some mitigations (eg. cache flush) are reversible, but cross-region DNS failover is not; system requires explicit confirm and a 5-minute hold window before action. Implementation plan: 1) Design throttling and prioritization rules and test on replayed production metrics (week 1). 2) Implement runbook generator lambda and template library, wire to service-catalog metadata (week 2). 3) Expose mitigations as signed actions behind RBAC and confirmation dialogs in the console (week 3). 4) Run staged canary: internal apps -> partner customers -> broad rollout (week 4). Rollout considerations: - Default to disabled for Dedicated and Private tenants; enable opt-in via console for first 2 weeks. - Provide a rollback toggle and metric dashboard. - Require runbook review sign-off from a reliability engineer and the owning service PM. Monitoring and metrics: - Pager count (by alert type), MTTA, MTTR, SLO breach rate, false positive rate. - Automation success/failure count, manual confirmations, and audit log volume. - Canary dashboards: staging traffic vs production. Operations runbook (high level): - When alert suppressed by throttling, page includes suppression reason and a link to the composed runbook. - For automated mitigation, create a placeholder incident with attached audit trail and require operator confirmation for cross-region failover. - Post-incident: automated evaluation runs comparing pre/post SLO and pushes runbook change suggestions to a drafts area for review. Links and artifacts: - Runbook generator design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/rb/RunbookGen-Design - Playbook templates repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks - Simulation dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/alerts/pager-throttle-sim - Proposed alert rules PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/alerts/pull/229 - Example incident after simulation: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-002 - Draft console UX comps: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/Redwood/Console/Runbook-Automation
